title: Finite quotient by a root of the prime parameter

statement: Let $R$ be a Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] normal domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] with fraction field $K$, and let $L/K$ be a finite field extension [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] in characteristic a prime $p$. Let $x\in R$ with $R/xR$ a domain and N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain]. Fix an integer $e\geq 0$ such that every $a\in L$ satisfies $a^{p^e}\in K$. Put $S=\operatorname{integralClosure}_R(L)$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure]. If $y\in S$ satisfies $y^{p^e}=x$, then $S/yS$ is a finitely generated $R$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module].

proof.text: If x=0, positivity of p^e gives y=0. Identify R/xR with R and their fraction fields. A finite-dimensional extension admits a small isomorphic model in the universe of R, so transport N-2 to that model and back to obtain that S=S/yS is finite over R.

source.place: Algebra, Tag 032P (lemma-tate-japanese), proof from the description of the prime yS through finiteness of S/yS; the zero-parameter case uses the definition of N-2

proof.text: Assume x is nonzero. Put q=p^e and let $\mathfrak p=xR$. The exponent q and the root y are given. *Basic properties of $S$.* $S$ is a subring of $L$ containing $R$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure], hence a domain, and by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal] $L$ is a fraction field of $S$. (a) For $f\in S$ we have $f^q\in R$: $f^q\in L^q\subseteq K$ is integral over $R$ (a power of an integral element; $S$ is a ring), and $R$ is integrally closed in $K$ by (1) [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. (b) $y\in S$, being a root of the monic $T^q-x\in R[T]$, and $y\neq0$ since $y^q=x\neq0$. (c) $xS\cap R=xR$: if $r=xs$ with $r\in R$, $s\in S$, then $s=r/x\in K$ is integral over $R$, so $s\in R$ by normality.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032P (lemma-tate-japanese, lines 45534-45589), proof: implicit in 'It is clear that q = {f ∈ S | f^q ∈ p} = yS since y^q = x' and in 'an element in the intersection has qth power contained in ∩x^nR'

proof.text: *The prime $\mathfrak q=yS$ over $\mathfrak p$ (the source's 'it is clear').* Put $\mathfrak q=yS$. Claim: for $f\in S$, $f\in\mathfrak q\iff f^q\in\mathfrak p$. If $f=ys$ ($s\in S$) then $f^q=xs^q\in xR$ since $s^q\in R$ by the power property above. Conversely if $f^q=xr$ with $r\in R$, then $g=f/y\in L$ satisfies $g^q=f^q/x=r\in R$, so $g$ is a root of the monic $T^q-r$ and $g\in S$, i.e. $f=yg\in yS$. Consequences: $1\notin\mathfrak q$ since $1\notin\mathfrak p$; if $fg\in\mathfrak q$ then $f^qg^q=(fg)^q\in\mathfrak p$ with $f^q,g^q\in R$, so as $\mathfrak p$ is prime $f^q\in\mathfrak p$ or $g^q\in\mathfrak p$, i.e. $f\in\mathfrak q$ or $g\in\mathfrak q$. So $\mathfrak q$ is a prime ideal of $S$. For $r\in R$: $r\in\mathfrak q\iff r^q\in\mathfrak p\iff r\in\mathfrak p$ ($\mathfrak p$ prime), so $\mathfrak q\cap R=\mathfrak p$. (The source deduces from Lemma 0BRA that $\mathfrak q$ is the unique prime over $\mathfrak p$; uniqueness is not used below, only that $yS$ is a prime lying over $\mathfrak p$, which is verified here directly.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032P (lemma-tate-japanese, lines 45534-45589), proof: 'there is a unique prime ideal q ⊂ S lying over the prime ideal p = xR. It is clear that q = {f ∈ S | f^q ∈ p} = yS since y^q = x'

proof.text: *$R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain.* $R_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is a local ring, a domain (a subring of $K$), and Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. Height of $\mathfrak p$: by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-height-quotient-bound] with $t=1$, $f_1=x$, $J=xR=\mathfrak p$ and $\mathfrak P=\mathfrak p$, $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)\le\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p/J)+1=\operatorname{ht}((0)\subset R/xR)+1=1$, the zero ideal having height $0$ (a chain of primes contained in $(0)$ has only the term $(0)$). And $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)\ge1$ by the chain $(0)\subsetneq\mathfrak p$ ($R$ is a domain, $\mathfrak p\ne0$). By [lem-weil-pbc-localization-dimension-chains-below-prime] the Krull dimension [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring] of $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is $\operatorname{ht}(\mathfrak p)=1$. (The source states here that $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a discrete valuation ring (00PD), and then that $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is Noetherian (Krull–Akizuki 00PG) and a discrete valuation ring; the rest of the proof uses only that $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is a one-dimensional Noetherian local domain, which is what Lemma 031F asks for, so these further assertions are not needed and not stated.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032P (lemma-tate-japanese, lines 45534-45589), proof: 'Observe that R_p is a discrete valuation ring by Lemma lemma-characterize-dvr. Then S_q is Noetherian by Krull-Akizuki ... a discrete valuation ring'

proof.text: *$\kappa(\mathfrak q)/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is finite.* Since $\mathfrak q\cap R=\mathfrak p$ (the prime and contraction description above), $R\setminus\mathfrak p\subseteq S\setminus\mathfrak q$, so the inclusion $R\subseteq S$ extends to an injective homomorphism of domains $\varphi:R_{\mathfrak p}\to S_{\mathfrak q}$, both rings being subrings of $L$ ($R_{\mathfrak p}\subseteq K$). The fraction field of $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is $K$, and that of $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is $L$, as $S\subseteq S_{\mathfrak q}\subseteq L$ and $L$ is a fraction field of $S$ [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal]; $\dim_KL<\infty$. The maximal ideal $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak qS_{\mathfrak q}$ satisfies $\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak n)=\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$: if $r/s\in\mathfrak qS_{\mathfrak q}$ with $r\in R$, $s\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$, write $r/s=f/t$ with $f\in\mathfrak q$, $t\in S\setminus\mathfrak q$; then $rt=sf\in\mathfrak q$ and $t\notin\mathfrak q$ give $r\in\mathfrak q\cap R=\mathfrak p$; the other inclusion is clear. By the local dimension calculation above, [lem-weil-pbc-dim-one-residue-field-extensions-finite] (3) applies to $\varphi$ and $\mathfrak n$: $\kappa(\mathfrak q)=S_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak qS_{\mathfrak q}$ is a finite-dimensional field extension of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)=R_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032P (lemma-tate-japanese, lines 45534-45589), proof: 'By Lemma lemma-finite-extension-residue-fields-dimension-1 we see that κ(q)/κ(p) is a finite field extension' (Tag 031F)

proof.text: *$S/yS$ is a finitely generated $R$-module.* By [lem-weil-pbc-prime-residue-field-algebra] (b), $R/\mathfrak p\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is injective and makes $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ a fraction field of the domain $R/\mathfrak p=R/xR$, and $S/\mathfrak q\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is injective; these maps are compatible with $R/\mathfrak p\to S/\mathfrak q$ and $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$. By the residue-field finiteness above and hypothesis (2) ($R/xR$ is N-2 [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain]), the integral closure $S'$ of $R/xR$ in $\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ [def-weil-pbc-integral-closure] is a finitely generated $R/xR$-module, hence a finitely generated $R$-module [lem-weil-pbc-finite-module-over-finite-algebra] ($R/xR$ is generated by $1$ as an $R$-module). Every element of $S/\mathfrak q$ is integral over $R/\mathfrak p$ (reduce modulo $\mathfrak q$ a monic equation over $R$ of a lift in $S$), so its image lies in $S'$: $S/yS=S/\mathfrak q$ is isomorphic to an $R$-submodule of $S'$, hence finitely generated over $R$ by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite].

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 032P (lemma-tate-japanese, lines 45534-45589), proof: 'Hence the integral closure S' ⊂ κ(q) of R/xR is finite over R/xR by assumption (2). Since S/yS ⊂ S' this implies that S/yS is finite over R'

theorem tate_root_closure_quotient_finite
    (R : Type u) (K L : Type v) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R]
    [Field K] [Field L] [Algebra R K] [IsFractionRing R K]
    [Algebra K L] [Algebra R L] [IsScalarTower R K L]
    [IsNoetherianRing R] (x : R) (hnormal : IsIntegrallyClosed R)
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] [CharP K p] [FiniteDimensional K L]
    [IsDomain (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({x} : Set R))]
    (hquot : IsN2 (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({x} : Set R))
      (FractionRing (R ⧸ Ideal.span ({x} : Set R))))
    (e : ℕ) (hpow : ∀ a : L, a ^ (p ^ e) ∈ (algebraMap K L).range)
    (y : integralClosure R L)
    (hy : y ^ (p ^ e) = algebraMap R (integralClosure R L) x) :
    Module.Finite R ((integralClosure R L) ⧸ Ideal.span ({y} : Set (integralClosure R L)))
